rows.text: # Processes: DNA isolation, PCR, gel electrophoresis, gene transfer ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Processes** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Biotechnology — Principles and Processes fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  The working processes of biotech: **DNA isolation** (lyse cells, remove proteins, precipitate pure DNA), **PCR** (polymerase chain reaction — amplify a DNA segment a billion-fold in hours using Taq polymerase through denaturation, primer annealing and extension cycles), **gel electrophoresis** (separate DNA fragments by size through an agarose gel — DNA is negative, so it runs to the anode), and **gene transfer**…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: DNA isolation: cell lysis (lysozyme/EDTA/detergent) → protease/RNase → chilled ethanol precipitation ('spooling') — the three-step order.  ·  Trick 2: PCR three steps: denaturation 94–95 °C, primer annealing 50–60 °C, extension 72 °C (Taq polymerase) — temperatures ARE the marks; 30 cycles ≈ 10⁹ copies.

Worked examples and applications ≥ 6 worked examples with solved steps, live examples and Nepal-context applications (biology-plan.md §3.1, block V) — written in the unit fill pass. ## 6. Key terms and statements Every new term defined once; exam-grade definitions live here and in keyPoints (block VI).  ·  **Worked example — PCR maths.** Starting with 1 copy and running 30 cycles: copies = 2³⁰ ≈ 1.07 billion. With 20 cycles: 2²⁰ ≈ 1 million. So the choice of cycle count sets sensitivity — forensic and diagnostic PCR use 30–40 cycles to detect vanishingly small starting amounts, which is also why contamination is fatal:…  ·  ## 7. (3) How does gel electrophoresis separate DNA, and which pole does DNA run toward? (4) Name four gene-transfer methods and one use each.…  ·  ## 8. Summary and self-check 5–10 line chapter summary, self-check questions and the common-confusions list (block VIII) — completed in the unit fill pass.  ·  **Summary.** Isolate, cut, amplify (PCR), check (gel), join, transfer — the standard pipeline of every cloning project. PCR's exponential maths and electrophoresis's size sorting are the two skills the exam loves. **Self-check:** can you state the three PCR temperatures and compute 2²⁰?
